clue.text: A daughter's befuddled, consuming large drinks

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so one piece takes another inside it
befuddled means confused, so the letters of the opening words are jumbled

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A young woman gets tipsy while knocking back big drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befuddled' turns A DAUGHTER'S (the 's counts as a letter here) into DRAUGHTAES, and 'consuming' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer drawn from a cask is draught ale, a kind of drink served in pubs.

clue.text: Breathless piper lacking expression

parts.note: someone no longer breathing is dead
Pan, the Greek god, plays the pipes

explanation.surface: A bagpiper out of puff can no longer show any feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The piper is Pan, the goat-footed god with his panpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face or delivery shows no emotion, keeping an impassive look.

clue.text: Current rock player

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: Someone who plays in a modern rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs a role on stage, a performer.

clue.text: No degrees at this London university?

definitions.text: No degrees at this London university?

parts.words: No degrees at this London university?
parts.note: the prime meridian of zero degrees longitude passes through this London district, home also to a university that does award degrees

explanation.surface: A sneer at a London college that apparently hands out no qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'degrees' are of longitude, not academic awards: the meridian line there marks zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The University of Greenwich is in south-east London, where the prime meridian, zero longitude, runs.

clue.text: Drawn and knotted

definitions.meaning: a drawn game ends level, with equal scores
something knotted has been fastened with a bow or knot

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a level match and a string bound into a knot.

clue.text: Meal done, ordered a drink

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dinner over, someone asks for something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing a request in a restaurant but signals rearranging MEAL DONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy or still citrus beverage, a soft drink.

clue.text: Plate of fish

parts.note: reads like a dish served at table, but means one of the small bony plates covering a fish's skin

explanation.surface: A dish of seafood on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' suggests crockery; here it is a protective flake on the fish itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish skin is covered with small overlapping protective plates, each one called by this name.

clue.text: It's divine embracing girl in time off

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: divine means holy, sacred
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A heavenly break: hugging a girlfriend on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a period away from work, a vacation.

clue.text: Fabric is produced for ready money only

parts.note: ready money is cash, money on hand
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: A cloth made strictly for paying customers who pay up front.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, woven into a luxury textile.

clue.text: In control of a race meeting taking two males fifty miles

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race meeting
he is a male, so two males give two copies of it
the second male, another he
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Running a racing event that involves two men covering fifty miles.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone steering a ship stands by the wheel, an idiom for being in charge.

clue.text: A number grow sick, get benefit

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
to ail is to become ill

explanation.surface: Several people fall ill, yet something good comes of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail oneself is to make use of something and profit by it.

clue.text: Mother and father split

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
rent means torn apart, split

explanation.surface: Mum and dad have separated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother and father' looks like one definition; only 'Mother' defines, and 'father' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother is to look after like a mum or dad would, so either noun or verb fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Engaged, that's the outcome about me and that girl

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: the end is the outcome
taken as written
she refers to that girl

explanation.surface: A man announces his engagement as the result of himself and his girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmeshed means caught up in, entangled, as gears are engaged.

clue.text: A complete fool can upset someone telling jokes

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word for can runs the other way in this down-free across clue

parts.note: a tin is a can
a wit is a clever, funny person

explanation.surface: An idiot can annoy the comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like 'annoy' with 'can' as a verb; in fact 'can' is a noun and 'upset' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Reckless injunction to keep increasing the rent

definitions.meaning: describes a wild, rash young person

definitions.text: injunction to keep increasing the rent
definitions.meaning: an order to carry on ripping, making the tear in the cloth bigger

explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is a tear in fabric, not money paid to a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a rash, unruly youngster; the phrase also urges continuing to rip.

clue.text: Affairs excluding union involvement

parts.note: sounds like trade-union business, but means romantic affairs outside the union of marriage

explanation.surface: Business matters handled without the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' is marriage, not a workers' organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidelity: sexual relations with someone other than one's spouse.

clue.text: Kill dead, accepting one pound

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: late means deceased
I is the Roman numeral one
a quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A hit paid for with a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: QUID is everyday British slang for £1.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate someone is to eliminate or murder them.

clue.text: Said sale is fixed and charged

indicators.note: fixed means rigged or rearranged, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: An auction allegedly rigged and someone prosecuted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' looks like a legal accusation, but means attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge at someone is to rush upon and attack them.

clue.text: Hurt during exam, leaves in this

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a test is an exam
to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: A student in pain mid-test walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wooden box used to ship loose tea is a container for those leaves.

clue.text: Outlaw to fight for food for children

parts.note: Friar Tuck is one of Robin Hood's outlaws
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A bandit takes on all comers to feed the young.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck box is the box of treats a British boarding-school child keeps; 'tuck' is school slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for a pupil's snacks at boarding school.

clue.text: Cry out — to the police?

definitions.meaning: to inform on someone to the police

explanation.definitionFit: Both a shrill cry and slang for informing to the authorities.

clue.text: Mid-evening in days before Easter can be quite mild

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: Lent is the forty days before Easter

indicators.note: Mid- picks the central letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A spring evening during the Lenten season can be fairly mild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mid-' takes the central three letters of 'evening', not just one, and 'in' places them after the first letter of the forty-day season.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means tolerant, gentle in punishment, not harsh.

clue.text: Applaud catch? Codswallop!

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
a trap is a catch

explanation.surface: Someone applauds a catch in cricket, then dismisses it as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious nonsense, rubbish talk.

clue.text: Note about fringe subject

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: te is a note in sol-fa
a hem is an edge or fringe

explanation.surface: A memo on the topic of the outer edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a topic, the subject matter of a talk.

clue.text: Hired assassin? Good show, old boy!

parts.note: a hit is a successful show
old man is a dated chummy form of address, like old boy

explanation.surface: A contract killer being congratulated: well done, old chap!
explanation.definitionFit: Someone paid to murder, a contract killer.

clue.text: Name I made up for a US State

indicators.note: made up means invented or composed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone invents a name for an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of the USA.

clue.text: Steal up around a wild beast

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Creeping up on a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild pig, a fierce untamed animal.

clue.text: Two support the Church

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pair of people back the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants.

clue.text: Appear to relish swallowing a double

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to look is to appear
to like is to relish

explanation.surface: Seeming to enjoy downing a double measure of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' looks like a drink; it means a person who looks exactly like another.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookalike is a doppelganger, someone resembling another closely.

clue.text: Insured drivers prefer to avoid backing like this

definitions.text: Insured drivers prefer to avoid backing like this

parts.words: Insured drivers prefer to avoid backing like this
parts.note: drivers dislike penalty marks on their licence, yet this word also means support or backing

explanation.surface: Motorists would rather not reverse in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, penalty points on a driving licence are called this, and raise insurance premiums; 'backing' suggests reversing a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Both approval or support and a penalty note on a driving licence.
